findings.F1: The tested signal is real but the book loses on fees: the bars stamped 15:00 and 16:00 gain +3.49 bp and +2.21 bp per held bar (15,205 and 16,018 bars), yet gross gain summed per coin-window is 0.061 against 0.134 in fees, because the position is opened and closed every day (Sharpe -1.98).
findings.F2: After a large 1-hour move a coin reverses, and more so when volatility is high: the slope of the next hour's return on the volatility-normalised 1-hour return rises steadily in size across 24-hour-volatility quintiles, from +0.17 bp (t 0.9) in the lowest to -7.46 bp (t -11.8) in the highest; on a non-overlapping 2-hour grid the highest tercile gives -9.41 bp (t -11.9, 68,851 cases).
findings.F3: That high-volatility reversal holds coin by coin and year by year: it is negative in all six coins (t from -1.87 for ETH to -6.60 for LTC) and in all eight years, significant in seven of them (2022 t -0.83).
findings.F4: Around midday UTC the 3-day trend reverses rather than continues: for the bar stamped 12:00 the slope of the 2-hour excess return on the 3-day standardised return is -5.89 bp (t -5.3, 16,829 cases); it is negative in all six coins (t from -0.68 to -4.46) and in seven of eight years, with five years at t ≤ -2.4; the neighbouring hours 11:00 (t -4.3) and 13:00 (t -3.4) agree.
findings.F5: Late in the UTC evening the 3-day trend continues: for the bar stamped 22:00 the slope is +5.61 bp (t 5.5, 16,778 cases), with 21:00 at t 3.1 and 23:00 at t 3.0; it is positive in all six coins (t from 1.6 to 2.9) and in seven of eight years.
findings.F6: The bars stamped 21:00 and 22:00 UTC rise on average by +5.5 bp (t 6.9) and +4.4 bp (t 5.8), positive in all six coins (t from 3.0 to 4.6) and in seven of eight years (2022: -2.2 bp, t -1.5).

ideas.idea: Over the next 2 hours, a coin moves against its last hour's return, and the move back is larger the larger that 1-hour return is relative to the coin's own 1-day volatility, most of all when that 1-day volatility is high.
ideas.consequence: In volatile hours, fade a sharp 1-hour spike in proportion to its size instead of chasing it.
ideas.name: high-volatility hourly spike reversal

ideas.idea: Over the 2 hours from 13:00 UTC, a coin moves against its own 3-day return, and the larger that 3-day return, the larger the move against it.
ideas.consequence: Lean against the 3-day trend in the early UTC afternoon rather than with it.
ideas.name: midday 3-day trend reversal

ideas.idea: Over the 2 hours from 23:00 UTC, a coin moves in the direction of its own 3-day return, and the larger that 3-day return, the larger the move with it.
ideas.consequence: Add with the 3-day trend late in the UTC evening, where the continuation is as strong as at the 16:00 settlement.
ideas.name: late-evening trend continuation
